narration.full_text: Control and coordination in animals are primarily provided by nervous and muscular tissues. The nervous tissue itself is an organized network of nerve cells, also known as neurons. These neurons are specialized for conducting information through electrical impulses from one part of the body to another. The nervous system is essentially a network of conducting tissues that receives stimuli and transmits them to various parts of the body. The fundamental units that make up this intricate system are called nerve cells or neurons. Receptors in our body gather information and pass it to the brain via a specific type of nerve cell known as sensory neurons. Conversely, motor neurons are responsible for transmitting information from the brain to effector organs, which are mainly muscles and glands, prompting a response. A nerve impulse is the information conveyed as chemical and electrical signals traveling through these neurons. These impulses are typically carried by dendrites towards the cell body of the neuron. The neuromuscular junction is a critical point where a muscle fibre comes into direct contact with a motor neuron. This motor neuron carries nerve impulses from the central nervous system. At this junction, impulses travel from the neuron to the muscle fibres using neurotransmitters, much like how impulses are transmitted across a synapse between two neurons. Voluntary actions are those that require conscious thought and are performed knowingly. These actions are under the control of our conscious mind. Examples include speaking to a friend or writing a letter. Involuntary actions, on the other hand, are not under the control of an individual's will. They are automatic responses to a stimulus and are not governed by the voluntary control of the brain. An example would be unknowingly touching a hot plate and immediately withdrawing your hand. A reflex action is a quick, sudden, and immediate response of the body to a stimulus. Common examples include the knee jerk reflex or the rapid withdrawal of a hand upon touching a hot object. The pathway through which a nerve impulse travels during a reflex action is known as a reflex arc.

visual_beats.description:
Text: Nervous System
- Control and coordination by nervous and muscular tissues.
- Nervous tissue: network of nerve cells (neurons), specialized for electrical impulses.

Text: Nervous System
- System of conducting tissues: receives stimulus, transmits to other parts.
- Units: Nerve cells or neurons.

Text: Types of Neurons
- Sensory neurons: Receptors pass info to brain.
- Motor neurons: Transmit info from brain to effector organs (muscles, glands).

Text: Nerve Impulse
- Information as chemical and electrical signals passing through neurons.
- Carried by dendrites towards cell body.

Text: Neuromuscular Junction
- Point where muscle fibre contacts motor neuron.
- Impulses travel from neuron to muscle via neurotransmitters (like synapse).

Text: Voluntary Action
- Actions needing thinking, performed knowingly.
- Controlled by conscious thought. E.g., Speaking, writing.

Text: Involuntary Action
- Not under conscious will, automatic response to stimulus.
- Not under voluntary brain control. E.g., Touching hot plate.

Image: Diagram of a reflex arc (IMAGE_1).
Text: Reflex Action
- Quick, sudden, immediate body response to stimulus. E.g., Knee jerk.
- Reflex arc: Pathway of nerve impulse during reflex action.

items: Control and coordination are provided by nervous and muscular tissues.
Nervous tissue is made up of an organized network of nerve cells or neurons, and it specialized for conduction information via electrical impulses from one part of the body to another.
Nervous system is the system of conducting tissues that receives the stimulus and transmits it to other parts of the body forming a network of nerves.
The units which makes up the nervous system are called nerve cells or neurons.
The receptors pass the information to the brain through a type of nerve cells called sensory neurons.
Motor neurons transmit the information from the brain to the effector organs, mainly muscles and glands.
Nerve Impulse: It is the information in the form of chemical and electrical signals passing through neurons. These impulses are carried by dendrites towards the cell body.

Neuromuscular Junction: It is the point where a muscle fibre comes in contact with a motor neuron carrying nerve impulses from the central nervous system. The impulses travel from the neuron to the muscle fibres by means of neurotransmitter in the same way as the transmission of impulses across a synapse between two neurons.
Voluntary Action: These are the actions which need thinking and are performed knowingly i.e. these are controlled by conscious thought. Example: Speaking to a friend, writing a letter etc.

Involuntary Action: These are not under the control of the will of an individual and are automatic response to a stimulus which is not under the voluntary control of the brain. Example: Touching a hot plate unknowingly.
